BUSINESS OF BIRTH

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
For 9 months you share one body, one breath. They are like the stranger you already know. The weeks, turn into months and you start to obsess about the day you will finally meet your baby. You vividly imagine what it will feel like to finally hold them, to see them in real life.
The last thing you think is that it will all end in the delivery room.

A midwife lead birth at a private birthing center is supposed to be a safe option for woman with uncomplicated pregnancies, to have natural childbirth.
But during our horrific investigation into the babies that died at Midwife Yolande Fouche’s birthing home, we realized business of birth has become a dangerous space, and these babies are the ones paying the price.

In this story we look at where we at, how we got here and we hold the midwives and SANC accountable

Script:


VO1
We're investigating private birthing homes, and a simple Google search shows 20 businesses offering midwife-led home deliveries in Gauteng and North West alone. Most have good reviews.

But, since our expose on a rogue midwife called Yolande Fouche, we've received tip-offs saying some are unsafe… even dangerous.

Masa on the phone – up sound

EMT CALL
This is not the first time that babies have been in distress when they were born in that institution
I was unconscious four times and they didn’t even care, my husband had to get me back
When she came out she wasn’t breathing

VO2
Inundated with reports of babies dying, we take a closer look - focusing on two facilities in particular.

FADE TO BLACK

VO3
First, we investigated Rustenburg’s Bingle Birth, from where midwife, Gladys Phakedi, performed home births until around 2 years ago

Anneke Jooste
I was thinking it would be safer and better at a midwife than at the state hospital.

VO4
Anneke’s Jooste’s first pregnancy had been a healthy one, and her doctor cleared her for a midwife-led delivery.

Half this up sound - SCANNING UPSOUND - OOO DAR IS DIE BABY - DIS GROOT

VO5
When her water broke in late December 2021, Anneke went to the birth house

AJ
when the midwife came, she said I was one centimetre dilated, and she said it was going to be a long night.
She seems like she wasn't very happy
Masa
Did it end up being a long night?
Anneke
Yes.

VO6
24 hours since Anneke's waters had broken, her labour hadn't progressed. As there was an increased risk of infection for the mother and baby, Phakedi should have followed established protocols and taken Anneke to the hospital.

Putting drip on

Instead … Phakedi put her on a drip, saying it would help with her low Iron. Within an hour, her labour ramped up dramatically.

AJ
So then they put me in the water. They said I was four centimetres, centimetres dilated.
she checked AGAIN. She said I'm eight centimetres.

VO7
Dr Margreet Wibbelink, a midwifery specialist, suspects that Phakedi had put an induction drug called oxytocin into the drip, leading to Anneke's accelerated labour.

MW
Inductions are a medical procedure that should never happen in a home birth setting
once you start interfering, the chances are that you need more interventions, whether it's some pain medication, or continuous monitoring to to see how the contractions are going, often times you will end up with a failed induction.
re needed, let's be in a hospital

VO8
Despite Anneke's healthy pregnancy and hopes for a gentle birth, things quickly spiralled out of control.
Her daughter WAS STUCK in the birth canal.


AJ
They said I don't push harder, are we going to lose her?

VO9
The delivery was extremely traumatic, but after hours of fighting, Gabriella was born just after 10 that night.

AJ
She wasn't breathing. She was blue, almost blackish.

VO10
Phakedi resuscitated and stabilised the baby and told Anneke an ambulance had been called. Hours passed, and no ambulance arrived.

AJ
we noticed, Gabriella's breathing started to go down. So my mom went to call them, andasked them where or the ambulance. Then the midwife told her that, no, they're so busy with paperwork.

masa on the case

VO11
This EMT who was on site that night says Phakedi called them almost three hours after the baby was born.

EMT CALL
We have had countless times that we go through to that place
They don’t call until they have no option

VO12
Anneke’s daughter died shortly after arriving at the hospital.

AJ
The doctor called us in and she passed away.
Anneke
But
I'm so sorry

VO13
An autopsy found evidence of acute oxygen deprivation as well as an injury to the baby’s head. Phakedi had used her hands to try and pull the baby out.

MW


I'm telling you this because I induced it.
00:34:31:18 - 00:34:37:15
Magriet
that's not proper home birthing midwife care at all.

They should just flip and say to keep their hands off the drugs.

VO14
Our investigation led us to another mother who, in 2017, had allegedly been given induction drugs to speed up labour and lost her baby at Phakedi’s practice. Her name is Lucinda Botes.

Masa on the phone – Hi Lucinda can you hear me
LB
She told me that the baby was too big and she was going to give me an induction so that I didn’t have to struggle
I was pushing for 4.5 hours constantly

VO15
Again, Phakedi transgressed her scope of practice by allegedly administering induction drugs and allowing prolonged labour instead of sending Lucinda to a state hospital. In the end, this baby girl pays the price.

LB
When she came out she was not breathing
When the paramedic arrived he said he can’t even start with CPR she has already passed away

VO 15 (b): Our Investigation turned to the second birthing home: Kathleen's Mother and Baby Clinic on Johannesburg's East Rand. It's owned by midwife, Kathleen van Heerden.



DOM
First, we did, like, an interview type of thing where we found out all the information
Kathleen did promise if anything does go wrong, these are backup OB. If there's an emergency, you get taken to a hospital.
photos of dom in the mirror


Dominique
The first, Blake kicked was the weirdest feeling in the world.
It feels like butterflies. Is your son forming into a human body, telling you, mommy, I'm here?


VO16
Dominique Van Den Berg's first pregnancy had been easy, and she looked forward to seeing the baby she'd carried for 9 months.
But a week before her due date, she felt off. BUT Each time she went to the birthing home, she was told she was fine and sent home. Then, one evening, she went in and was seen by Kathleen’s assistant.

Dominique
she said to me, You are two centimeters dilated. I'm going to break your water so you can leave with your baby today. So we don't have any false alarms anymore, She breaks my water. The first thing that comes out of her mouth is the ocean. Like, what do you mean? I should, like, be in the streets. I'm like, what do you mean, no? Your water is broken. I need to find the ambulance.

VO18
The baby had passed its meconium in the abiotic fluid, which is a sign of distress. According to protocol, Dominique should have been referred to a hospital, but instead, it seems she was induced.

Dominique
she told me. I'm going to give you a tablet now. Drink it now and then. In 20 minutes, I'll give you the other half.
It's just to help you get your contractions faster and get you to dilate first because of, like, being in the streets.

VO19
This appears to suggest the administering of the induction drug Cytotec - again, something midwives are not allowed to do in a home birth setup as it's extremely dangerous. It over-stimulates the uterus, giving no space for the baby to breathe.

DOM
I started getting more and more contractions as it went on.
they had me on this thing you put over your tummy.
Every time Blake's heartbeat went under a certain beat, the machine went off.

VO20
According to Dominique’s mother, the baby's heart rate dropped, and he was clearly in distress. She insisted they go to the hospital. But Kathleen argued they would need to pay 220 thousand rand to the hospital upfront

DOM
Kathleen was running around between me and the other mom. She eventually got there when we told her to take us to the hospital. Is it critical that we need to buy 220,000 rate for what?
Before they're going to help me?
Masa
In hindsight, knowing what you know now, why do you think she mentioned 200,000.

DOM
so that I can stay there and so that she can have my money? Because if it is that you do give birth and it was in a contract, if you give birth that she needs to give you your money back.
Masa
You think this was a money decision?
Dominique
Definitely, definitely.

VO21
Aware of the dangers of induction drugs, it was hard to understand why these midwives - the custodians of safe and sacred births - acted as they did. Could it be about the money?

MASA
Do you think that there is a move to creating this, to being a business of birthing, as opposed to the focus on mommy and child care?
Magriet
Look, there's medical bills to pay. So there is a business element to this. But I personally think it's unethical to try to want to make money on babies, and that unfortunately happens too much. Yes, a doctor needs to be well enumerated and a midwife to let us pay decent remuneration, but don't try to make it a business to catch as many babies that you can have.
that you can earn a lot of money.


VO22
Clariza Van Nieuwenheizen, who delivered with Kathleen in 2021, was also allegedly given induction drugs.

CVN
she gave me a pull. she said, only allowed to give me half a pill. It helps for the contraction. But she gave me a full one because my water is already broken.
Masa
She didn't say she's using a drug to induce that thing.
Clarissa
She only said to me that it's for the contractions to help the labor. That's all she said.

VO23
Clariza's medical records, obtained from Kathleen, show that at 24 hours when she should have been transferred, she was given Oxytocin to induce labour. And, as with the other babies we'd heard about, Clariza’s went into distress.

CVN
my mother, my grandmother decided, I have to go to hospital. Otherwise this baby's not gonna make it.
And Kathleen was like, no, no, no, trying to stop it.
as soon as we got in the car, she was standing next to the car and she said to us, you did not pay.
So my husband showed her the proof of payment of the 15,000 paid
Masa
So we must wait for this. And while you are in active labor,
Clarissa
told my grandmother, you know what?
Clarissa
The pain is so bad. I'd just rather want to die

bridge

As soon as we got to the hospital, the nurse told me, your baby's in distress.
And the doctor said if you were 30 minutes late, your baby would have died.

c-section video - baby comes out - up sound



VO 24
Clariza’s son Colton was safely delivered via emergency c-section.

Baby cries

But Dominique's story didn’t have a happy ending. Kathleen delivered BLAKE on the 16 of May, and he died soon afterwards.

DOM
They wanted to play God
I don't I don't wish this on anyone to see you, son.
Turning blue next to you

Autopsy
The autopsy report made various findings in keeping with acute asphyxia or a lack of oxygen

VO 25
We emailed Kathleen, but she refused to speak to us, citing legal reasons. Unwilling to leave it there, we went to her birthing home, but again, she refused to talk to us. So, we tried calling.

VO 26 - Kathleen told us to approach the SA Nursing Council, the regulatory body for midwives, for answers.

MASA ON THE PHONE - We have evidence that you are using induction drugs and she hangs up – end on the hang up

Anneke
They say it gets easier. I don't think so. Sometimes, you relive it like you're in that moment again, and that is the worst.

VO 27
Our investigation into Midwife Gladys Phakedi showed that 6 babies died in her care between 2016 and 2022. We tried repeatedly to contact her, but she never responded. Bingle Birth told us that she rented birth space from them and the clients were hers, not theirs.


In 2023, three complaints against Phakedi were sent to the South African Nursing Council or SANC but the families say they haven’t even received an acknowledgement email.

Magriet
We need a bit more rules and regulations in place to make this a safe, profitable business.

SANC admitted they don't actively go out. They wait until something goes wrong at one of these birthing centers in some of the larger ones as a formal complaint, and only then will they look into it.
Magriet
Correct.
MASA
So basically nobody's really auditing or checking these birthing centers.
Magriet
Correct. There's a systemic issue here. If we continue to do the same things, we will see more problems.

VO28
The Nursing Council initially refused to talk to us, but later sent a written response after we approached the National Department of Health.
SANC is currently investigating Gladys Phakedi, who is still a registered nurse.

On Kathleen Van Heerden, Dominique says she first submitted her complaint in March 2021. But SANC denies this, saying they first received the complaint this year, and that Kathleen is currently under investigation.

Dominique
I know we live in a country. People don't pay for their sins, but I want them to pay.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: For 9 months you share one body, one breath. They are like the stranger you already know. The weeks, turn into months and you start to obsess about the day you will finally meet your baby. You vividly imagine what it will feel like to finally hold them, to see them in real life. The last thing you think is that it will all end in the delivery room. A midwife lead birth at a private birthing center is supposed to be a safe option for woman with uncomplicated pregnancies, to have natural childbirth. But during our horrific investigation into the babies that died at Midwife Yolande Fouche’s birthing home, we realized business of birth has become a dangerous space, and these babies are the ones paying the price. In this story we look at where we at, how we got here and we hold the midwives and SANC accountable
